title: SLO Steward Rotation and Capacity Handoff Manual
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:

This document defines the SLO Steward rotation pattern, a formal capacity handoff protocol, and the associated artifacts required to safely transfer operational responsibility for service SLOs and error budgets between teams. It bridges oncall practices, capacity planning, and SRE reliability initiatives so that ownership transitions preserve headroom, evidence context, and recovery plans.

Why this matters:
- SLOs and error budgets are operational contracts; ad-hoc handoffs cause missed mitigation windows and incorrect throttling decisions.
- Inference workloads are bursty and heterogeneous; capacity state and quantization/instance profiles must be explicitly communicated.
- A predictable stewarding process reduces escalations, accelerates recovery, and preserves customer trust.

Scope and intent:
- Applies to all model-serving and multi-tenant inference services (hosted, dedicated, private) managed by eng-sre and runtime teams.
- Covers regular rotation (shift changes), planned handoffs for maintenance/change windows, and emergency ownership transfers during incidents.
- Does not replace per-service runbooks; it references them and prescribes required artifacts for handoff.

Definitions:
- SLO Steward: the oncall or designated engineer responsible for SLO health, error-budget decisions, and capacity handoffs for a given service window.
- Capacity Headroom: the measurable spare token-processing capacity based on GPU pool sizing + warm pools. Expressed as percent of provisioned throughput.
- Error Budget Reserve: the currently available budget (in % of allowed SLI violation) allocated for planned experiments or absorbable incidents.
- Handoff Artifact: required context items (see checklist) shared at rotation or handover time.

Required artifacts for every handoff (Handoff Checklist):
1) Current SLO status snapshot (quantile latencies, availability, daily burn rate)
2) Error budget remaining and 7d trend
3) Capacity headroom (%), largest tenants consuming capacity, and recent allocation changes
4) Open mitigations and active throttles/fallbacks (routes, model fallbacks)
5) Recent synthetic canary failures and their ticket/PR links
6) Known upcoming events (deploys, batch jobs, scheduled migrations)
7) Contact list: owner, escalation chain, support rotation for dependent services
8) Runbook links and reproduction harness commands

Handoff schedule and cadence table (example):
| Frequency | Who initiates | Minimum handoff window | Ownership record | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| Daily rotation | Outgoing steward | 10 minutes | Slack message + Handoff doc | Include last 1-hour telemetry snapshot |
| Pre-maintenance | Change owner | 30 minutes | Jira change + capacity check | Tag oncall and capacity-orch channel |
| Emergency transfer | Incident commander | Immediate | Incident channel + evidence bundle | Follow emergency transfer steps below |

Operational tooling integrations:
- PagerDuty escalation profile: "SLO-Stewards" (priority -> pager)
- Slack channels: #sre-stewards, #capacity-orchestration, #model-serve-incidents
- Capacity Orchestrator (cap-orch) API endpoints used in handoffs: GET /v1/headroom, POST /v1/evict, POST /v1/eviction-preview
- Telemetry dashboards: per-model SLI dashboard (latency p50/p95/p99), error-budget burn rate chart, tenant-heatmap

Standard handoff procedure (regular rotation):
1) Outgoing steward populates the Handoff Checklist document (template below) and posts to #sre-stewards.
2) Outgoing shares a 10-minute verbal summary with incoming steward: current SLO state, active mitigations, and capacity pressures.
3) Incoming verifies live dashboards and runs the quick verification commands (examples below).
4) If incoming detects a discrepancy > 10% headroom variance or >20% error budget change from the snapshot, escalate to the service owner and delay handoff.
5) Record the handoff in the rotation log with timestamp and artifacts attached (link to checklist).

Emergency ownership transfer (incident-driven):
1) Incident commander declares transfer and assigns new SLO Steward in the incident channel.
2) Outgoing steward pushes an evidence bundle (last 1 hour traces, top 5 slow traces, eviction events) to the incident docket.
3) Incoming steward runs the incident triage checklist and confirms control planes for throttling and fallback are available.
4) If capacity change is required, call cap-orch emergency API and update incident timeline.

Quick verification commands (examples):
- Verify headroom: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://cap-orch.internal/v1/headroom?service=model-serving | jq .headroom_percent
- Error budget snapshot: curl -s https://slo-metrics.internal/api/v1/snapshot?service=model-serving | jq .error_budget_remaining
- Canary status: kubectl -n serve get pods -l app=canary -o jsonpath='{.items[*].status.phase}'

Thresholds and decision matrix:
| Signal | Threshold | Immediate action | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| Headroom <= 15% | <= 15% provisioned | Initiate emergency capacity request; enable throttling | SLO Steward + CapOps |
| Error budget burnrate > 2x baseline | 2x sustained for 1 hour | Pause risky experiments; escalate to incident command | SLO Steward |
| P99 latency increase > 40% | relative to 7d median | Verify deployment, check hot cache, run warm-pool refill | Runtime team |
| Canary failures >= 3 in 15m | 3 failures | Halt rollout; rollback candidate | Platform owner |

Handover message template (Slack):
"Handoff: model-serving | Outgoing: @aisha | Incoming: @marco | SLO: availability 99.95% | Headroom: 22% | ErrorBudget: 68% | Active mitigations: throttling to tiered lanes; canary paused | See docs: <link>"

Evidence and archival policy:
- Attach handoff checklist and 1-hour evidence snapshot to the daily rotation log. Retain rotation logs for 90 days.
- Incident-driven transfers: append evidence bundle to incident record; retention per incident policy (1 year for Sev2+, 90 days for Sev3+).
- For audits: export CSV of rotation logs and handoff artifacts on quarterly cadence.

Training and rollout:
- All stewards must complete a 1.5-hour training: overview, simulator lab, emergency transfer drill.
- New rotation members shadow outgoing stewards for two full rotations before independent handoffs.
- Bi-annual tabletop: run a cross-team capacity handoff exercise and record metrics (handoff time, missed signals).

Post-handoff review and KPIs:
- KPIs to track: average handoff duration, % of handoffs with complete checklist, incidents arising within 2 hours of handoff, mean time to stabilization after emergency transfer.
- Review cadence: SRE leadership reviews KPIs monthly; improvements are tracked as reliability initiatives.

Appendix A — Handoff checklist template (copyable):
- Service: 
- Steward outgoing: 
- Steward incoming: 
- Timestamp: 
- SLO snapshot (p50/p95/p99 latency, availability): 
- Error budget remaining (current, 7d trend): 
- Capacity headroom (% and top 5 tenants): 
- Active mitigations and where configured (route ids): 
- Recent deploys and canary status: 
- Open tickets/PRs relevant to runtime: 
- Links: dashboards, runbooks, incident channel 

Appendix B — Example: planned maintenance handoff checklist excerpt:
- Scheduled maintenance window: 2024-06-23 22:00–23:00 UTC
- Expected cap reduction: 18% while nodes reboot
- Pre-approved reserve: +10% burst allocation requested via cap-orch ticket #CO-442
- Mitigation plan: pre-warm caches, enable fallback small-model variant, notify customers with high-traffic flag

Ownership and escalation:
- Primary: SLO Steward (oncall)
- Secondary: Runtime owner (team runtime)
- Tertiary: ENG-SRE Lead (pager)

Document maintenance:
- Owner: eng-sre (stewardship working group)
- Review cadence: annually or after any handoff-related incident resulting in customer impact
- Change process: PR to this page with at least two reviewers from SRE + Runtime

Contact and resources:
- Slack: #sre-stewards (operational), #capacity-orchestration (capacity ops)
- PagerDuty: SLO-Stewards escalation policy
- Templates: /docs/rotation-templates/handoff-checklist.md

End of document.
